# Nimzo

> Nimzo turns your infrastructure policies and best practices into deterministic checks that every change passes, whoever or whatever writes it.

This file is generated from the site's source content. It is a curated index for AI assistants, not a crawler permissions file. For crawler permissions, see `/robots.txt`.

## Core Pages

- [Home](https://nimzo.com/): Primary overview of the site.

## Blog

- [Blog index](https://nimzo.com/blog): Practical guides on Terraform, policy as code and IaC security.
- [How to review a Terraform plan before you apply](https://nimzo.com/blog/how-to-review-terraform-plan): How to review a Terraform plan: save it with -out, read the +, -, ~ and -/+ symbols, catch replacements and destroys, and check terraform show -json.
- [IaC scanning compared: Checkov, tfsec, KICS, Terrascan](https://nimzo.com/blog/iac-security-scanners-compared): IaC scanning compared: Checkov, tfsec, KICS, Terrascan and Trivy. Rule formats, coverage, maintainers and current status, plus which scanner to choose.
- [Open Policy Agent (OPA) for Terraform: a practical guide](https://nimzo.com/blog/open-policy-agent-terraform): Learn how to use Open Policy Agent with Terraform: export plan JSON, write Rego rules, run Conftest in CI, and unit test your policies before apply.
- [Terraform validate vs TFLint vs policy checks](https://nimzo.com/blog/terraform-validate-vs-tflint): TFLint, terraform validate and policy checks catch different problems. See what each one finds and where to run it: locally, in pre-commit, or in CI.
- [What is policy as code? Examples and tools](https://nimzo.com/blog/what-is-policy-as-code): Policy as code turns security and compliance rules into code that checks every change. See real examples and compare OPA, Conftest, Kyverno and Sentinel.
